intro: A mixture model does not know which component generated each observation. One EM step turns current likelihoods into soft assignments and updates component statistics.
task: Perform one full univariate Gaussian-mixture expectation and maximization step, returning updated parameters and the old total log likelihood.
requirements: values is a vector. weights, means, and variances are equal-length component vectors; weights sum to one and are strictly positive. Variances and variance_floor lie in [1e-8,1e6].
Compute normalized responsibilities using log Gaussian density plus log weight. Use responsibility sums for new weights, weighted means, and weighted population variances about the new means.

Return {"weights": new_weights, "means": new_means, "variances": maximum(new_variances,variance_floor), "log_likelihood": sum(old log evidence)}. Reject any component effective count <=1e-12; do not relabel components.

Use real finite numeric inputs with magnitude at most 1e6, excluding booleans. Vectors have length 1..128 and matrix axes have length 1..128 unless a tighter bound is stated. Leave all inputs unchanged; raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Find the structure
hints.body: Calculate log joint component scores and normalize each observation row after subtracting its largest score.

hints.title: Build the calculation
hints.body: Use fractional memberships to compute new means first, then center the variance calculation on those new means.

explanation: The expectation step normalizes component joint densities into responsibilities. The maximization step treats those responsibilities as fractional membership weights for new means and variances.
The likelihood belongs to the parameters supplied at the start of the step. A variance floor prevents collapse to zero width; numerically empty components require a policy and are rejected here.
